questions: Q1: How should the CLI commands for netsuite and run integrate with the existing hlx CLI structure?
Q2: How should the CLI handle environment defaults and override?
Q3: Should hlx run be a top-level command or under inspect?

answers.answer: Two new handler files follow the established db.ts/logs.ts pattern: netsuite.ts (60 lines) as a subcommand of 'inspect' with query/logs modes, and run/index.ts (53 lines) as a top-level command. Both use resolveRepo, getFlag, getPositionalArgs, and hxFetch. Verified: netsuite case at inspect/index.ts lines 125-138, run case at index.ts lines 101-105. Both import with .js extensions (ES module convention).
evidence: src/inspect/netsuite.ts — 60 lines, cmdNetsuite handler, query/logs modes via POST to /{repoId}/netsuite
src/run/index.ts — 53 lines, cmdRun handler, --repo/--env/--code/--modules via POST to /{repoId}/run
src/inspect/index.ts lines 125-138 — netsuite case in router switch
src/index.ts lines 101-105 — run case in main dispatcher

answers.answer: Both handlers read /tmp/helix-inspect/manifest.json for nsDefaultEnv (set by orchestrator per step). Mapping: PRODUCTION->'prod', else->'sandbox'. The --env flag overrides the manifest default. Graceful fallback: if manifest is unreadable (try/catch), env defaults to undefined (server resolves to SANDBOX). Verified: readManifestDefaultEnv function at netsuite.ts lines 7-18 and run/index.ts lines 7-18 (identical implementation).
evidence: src/inspect/netsuite.ts line 24 — const env = envFlag ?? readManifestDefaultEnv()
src/run/index.ts line 30 — const env = envFlag ?? readManifestDefaultEnv()

answers.answer: hlx run is a top-level command (not hlx inspect run). The server route is POST /api/inspect/:repoId/run (under inspect for auth simplicity), but the CLI command is top-level to reflect the fundamentally different governance model: inspect netsuite is read-only by construction, run allows arbitrary SuiteScript. Verified: case 'run' in src/index.ts main dispatcher (lines 101-105), handler at src/run/index.ts.
evidence: src/index.ts lines 101-105 — case 'run' in main dispatcher, imports cmdRun from ./run/index.js
src/run/index.ts — handler in its own directory, not under inspect/
RSH-636 AD-6 — hlx run allows arbitrary SuiteScript, no assertReadOnlyQuery (different governance)

statement: The helix-cli changes are a thin interface layer (~4 files, ~113 lines of new code) following established CLI patterns. Two new handlers (cmdNetsuite, cmdRun) read environment defaults from the inspection manifest, use hxFetch for HTTP dispatch, and output JSON to stdout. hlx run is top-level (not under inspect) to reflect its distinct governance model. No new dependencies, zero architectural risk.
